name: Stone's Throw
description:
Mount Ardis looks out of place. It is as if the edge of something great and alien has broken through the earth, pointing threateningly skyward. It glowers over the lesser, gray, crumbling peaks and foothills around it and its uncanny black surface seems to devour the light that falls upon it. It is as magnetic as it is imposing, and maybe that's why the town of Stone's Throw sprang up at its feet.

Walking its switchbacking streets, among buildings built nearly on top of one another, it is evident that its boom-time has passed. Signs for shops and taverns seem a bit too eager for business. The mountain guides now offer only weekly excursions to the summit. The few tourists who do trickle in are set upon from all sides with offers of lodgings, vittles and entertainment, but the greater part of the locals can be seen simply lazing about, as if waiting for something to change the town's fortune.

The mountain itself, though, is ever-changing. Caves explored once are often found to have changed their course when visited again. Mysterious, sourceless landslides of previously-unknown minerals are found at the mountain's feet. Stream beds are full of ore one day and empty of it the next. And every local will tell you that when you lie in bed at night, there is a great, unceasing grinding below - as of worlds colliding - that you can feel more than hear.

hooks.name: The Rune Quarry
hooks.description: The mountain was especially restless last night, and this morning a large landslide was found to have tumbled down the mountainside, revealing an ancient quarry of rune-carved blocks of stone. One of the mountaineers who came across the quarry badly burned his hand somehow by touching one of the runes. Another thought they saw a shadowy shape appear nearby when they touched another rune. Local lore contains no record of any quarry nearby, and the runes bear no resemblance to any language or iconography currently in use.
hooks.gmNotes:
Should Our Heroes investigate the quarry, they should be immediately set upon by the shadowy creature. The quarry should be an interactive arena of triggerable rune effects - some helpful, some harmful - in which the battle can take place.

Further investigation should allow Our Heroes to find a way (via runes) to access a hidden chamber. Here there should be a pictographic narrative showing some unknown race worshipping a mountain that looks a lot like Mount Ardis. The images should suggest that these people used the mountain as some sort of portal, which of course Our Heroes may also do if they can figure out how to operate the runes in the chamber.

Where the chamber takes them is up to you. Perhaps it takes them through time, and they emerge in the environs of Mount Ardis, but in some far-distant time (Future or past? If the former, consider archaeological evidence of Stone's Throw). Or perhaps the mountain is a conduit between planes of existence.

Either way, there should be an immediate sense of wonder at their new surroundings, followed immediately by some disaster that cuts them off from or destroys the portal chamber, so that they must figure out how to get back.

hooks.name: The Rock Kingdom
hooks.description:
An elderly mountain guide, Erasmus, haunts the streets of Stone's Throw with his ceaseless rambling. Among many other tales, he claims to have become lost in a tunnel that led deep inside the mountain, where he encountered a kingdom of towering humanoid creatures of living, moving stone. As he tells it, he remained there for years and ultimately led a rebellion against a cruel crystal king, before deciding to return to the outside world.

Other locals scoff at the story, though they admit Erasmus did go missing for a few years a while back. Erasmus himself will tell you his story is true and that anyone brave enough to explore the caves and tunnels of the mountain can find the kingdom, just as he did. Then he will turn and walk away, pop a pebble into his mouth, chew and swallow.
hooks.gmNotes:
A cave explore can go awry when the mountain shifts while they are in it, cutting off their escape to the surface but opening new tunnels that lead deeper. Some dramatic mishap should be the thing that leads Our Heroes to Erasmus' rock kingdom: a sudden collapse of a span across a chasm or similar will do. There should be a sense of "this is the end for us."

They fall or slide or whatever you choose into the rock kingdom, landing on or near a pair of humanoid rock creatures - one large and stoic, the other small and talkative.

From here the adventure is whatever you care to make it. Perhaps it's completely different from Erasmus' tale, perhaps it's a repetition, with a cruel king in need of overthrowing, etc. (in which case, perhaps some details of Erasmus' story provide useful hints as the adventure continues).

Whatever the climax, the denouement should be Our Heroes trying to figure out how to get back to the surface. Perhaps there is some rock deity who will transport them - for a fee. Or perhaps their deeds earn them the services of the stone people, who open a way for them.

If your group can stomach it, you could opt for the "it was all a dream" route, where they awake to find they had been knocked unconscious at the bottom of the long fall or whatever calamity you chose to mark the beginning of the rock kingdom adventure, among a grove of spore-producing plants, near a crack venting gases or some other obvious apparent cause for a hallucination. However, as they make their way out of the mountain, perhaps one of them realizes they still have some token of their time in the rock kingdom with them, and perhaps another - without realizing it - has begun snacking on pebbles.

hooks.name: River Rescue
hooks.description:
A dignitary from a seafaring nation was deep in his cups last night at one of the lodges when he got into an argument with a local over whether a sea sailor could navigate a river. His pride on the line, he proclaimed that he would prove his boat mastery this very night. Against the protests and warnings of locals, the dragged a canoe to the edge of the river, leaped in, and set off with a single paddle.

The river below Stone's Throw is a deathtrap of rapids, falls and whirlpools that even the most seasoned river sailors would find nearly impossible to navigate. Word has spread that the man's errand in Stone's Throw was to procure a great quantity of gems on behalf of the royal house he serves - a task which he had completed earlier in the day.

Now, those gems are either on his person or settling into the silt of the river bottom - or both. The reward for his rescue might equal the value of the gems besides. Either way, groups of search parties are forming, and it seems the race is on to find what remains of this foolish man.
hooks.gmNotes:
This can go a couple different ways.

For one, you could make it more about the race between search parties, as well as the challenge of traversing the terrain and/or the river. Perhaps conflict arises when multiple groups arrive at the scene of the man's demise at the same time.

Or perhaps the man secretly used water-shaping or flight magic to safely transport himself below the dangerous part of the river. Our Heroes can find him safe and sound, but the problem should arise that some of the search parties are determined to kill him if they find him alive, so they can take the gems. The challenge then becomes escorting this man to safety, with a generous reward at the end of the task.
